;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Six people are killed and twenty others injured after an [[al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] [[suicide bomber]] blew himself up outside a mosque in [[Kismayo]], [[Somalia]]. The target of the attack is suspected to be a local politician. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/09/killed-suicide-bombing-mosque-somalia-200911152954557.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[September 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Two civilians and two soldiers are killed and 13 other people are injured during a bombing attack at a wedding in [[Khost]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://tolonews.com/index.php/afghanistan/four-killed-khost-wedding-blast (TOLONews)]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)]]
**Security forces kill at least four leaders from the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]] in [[Samarra District]], [[Iraq]]. [http://ninanews.com/Website/News/Details?key=855925 (National Iraqi News Agency)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] signs into law the [[Bayanihan to Recover as One Act]], a [[Philippine peso|₱]]165.5 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]3.4 billion) stimulus package to extend the [[Bayanihan to Heal as One Act]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2020-09-11/philippines-duterte-signs-34-billion-pandemic-stimulus-package-into-law (Reuters via U.S. News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****The [[Ministry of Interior (Thailand)|interior ministry]] announces plans to convert [[Border Patrol Police]] camps into [[quarantine]] facilities in order to accommodate additional [[migrant workers]] as part of an effort to address [[Thailand|the country]]'s [[labour shortage]] caused by the pandemic. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-09/11/c_139361436.htm (Xinhua)]
**[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the restaurant industry in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****It is announced that bars in [[South Florida]] counties such as [[Miami-Dade County, Florida|Miami-Dade]] and [[Palm Beach County, Florida|Palm Beach County]] will remain closed. However, bars in the rest of the [[Florida|state]] will be allowed to reopen at a 50% capacity. [https://www.sun-sentinel.com/local/broward/fl-ne-south-florida-bar-closures-20200911-r6dtuipsq5blpam3hmseomnx44-story.html (''The Sun-Sentinel'')] [https://www.nydailynews.com/coronavirus/ny-coronavirus-florida-bars-reopen-fifty-percent-capacity-20200911-gnnfiansgneclcbuosajq674xu-story.html (''New York Daily News'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*A cave-in at a [[Mining industry of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|gold mine]] near [[Kamituga]] in [[South Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], kills at least 50 miners. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/sep/11/at-least-50-killed-in-collapsed-gold-mine-in-east-congo-says-ngo (''The Guardian'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****It is announced that schools in [[Los Angeles County, California|Los Angeles County]] will remain closed until the winter. [https://patch.com/california/los-angeles/la-schools-stay-closed-until-least-november (Patch.com)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado]]
*****[[Governor of Colorado|Governor]] [[Jared Polis]] says that the state might extend its [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] in indoor public spaces for another 30 days. [https://www.denverpost.com/2020/09/11/colorado-mask-order-extension/ (''The Denver Post'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****[[Michigan]] records 1,313 new cases, its highest single-day total since April 24. [https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2020/09/michigan-reports-highest-one-day-spike-in-coronavirus-cases-since-april.html (MLive.com)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****For the second time in the same week, [[Portugal]] reports the biggest daily increase in new cases since the national [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] was lifted in May, with 687 new cases and three deaths, bringing the cumulative totals to 62,813 confirmed cases and 1,855 deaths in 193 days since the first infections were detected in the country. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/193_DGS_boletim_20200911.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] reports 108 new cases, an all-time high. [https://www.rtvslo.si/zdravje/novi-koronavirus/od-nedelje-vse-karantene-po-10-dni-ijs-povprecje-dnevnih-okuzb-bo-pocasi-narascalo/535780 (RTVSLO)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 3,539 cases of COVID-19, up from 2,919 a day earlier. Six deaths are also reported. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-britain-cases-idUSKBN2622DB (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City]]
****[[Vatican City|Vatican]]-based [[Philippines|Filipino]] [[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|cardinal]] [[Luis Antonio Tagle]], the [[Prefect]] of the [[Congregation for the Evangelization of Peoples]], tests positive for COVID-19. [https://wtvbam.com/2020/09/11/vatican-based-filipino-cardinal-tests-positive-for-coronavirus/ (Reuters via WTVB)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan]]
***The number of recoveries in [[Kyrgyzstan]] reaches past 40,000. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-09/11/c_139361691.htm (Xinhua)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Namibia]]
***The [[Hosea Kutako International Airport]] in [[Windhoek]], [[Namibia|the country]]'s main international airport, reopens to international flights after a six-month closure. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-09/11/c_139361881.htm (Xinhua)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[Brazil]]ian [[states of Brazil|state]] of [[Bahia]] is expected to conduct phase III trails of [[Russia]]'s [[Gam-COVID-Vac]] [[vaccine]] and buy 50 million doses. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-russia-brazil-idUSKBN2613NH (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[Japan–United Kingdom relations]], [[Impact of Brexit]]
**[[Japan]] and the United Kingdom reach a tentative [[free trade agreement]], which [[Secretary of State for International Trade|British trade secretary]] [[Liz Truss]] hails as the UK's "first major post-[[Brexit]] trade deal". [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/09/11/uk-and-japan-agree-on-principle-to-free-trade-deal.html (CNBC)]
*[[Bahrain–Israel normalization agreement]]
**[[Israel]] and [[Bahrain]] agree to establish relations. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/trump-expected-to-announce-historic-bahrain-israel-normalization-agreement-641961 (''Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[China–United States relations]]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China|Chinese foreign ministry]] announces it would [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocate]] the sanctions that the [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] imposed earlier this month onto its senior diplomats visiting the U.S., by also imposing similar countermeasures to U.S. diplomats in China. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/beijing-china-restrictions-us-diplomats-tiktok-huawei-trump-13103420 (AFP via CNA)]

;Law and crime
*[[1989 murders of Jesuits in El Salvador]]
**A court in [[Madrid]] sentences former [[El Salvador|Salvadoran]] deputy minister for public security Inocente Orlando Montano Morales to 133 years in prison for the [[murder]]s of six [[Jesuit]]s and two others in [[San Salvador]] during [[Salvadoran Civil War|the country's civil war]] in 1989. [https://www.vanguardngr.com/2020/09/spain-sentences-76-year-old-soldier-to-133-years-for-murdering-five-priests/ (AFP via ''Vanguard'')]
*A court in [[Turkey]] sentences opposition parliamentarian [[Remziye Tosun]] of the pro-[[Kurds in Turkey|Kurdish]] [[Peoples' Democratic Party (Turkey)|Peoples' Democratic Party]] (HDP) to ten years in prison for "membership in a [[terrorism in Turkey|terrorist]] organization" and "treating wounded [[Kurdistan Workers' Party]] (PKK) members" during clashes in 2016. Her lawyer rejects the verdict. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-security-lawmaker/turkish-court-sentences-pro-kurdish-mp-to-jail-on-terrorism-charges-idUSKBN2621VJ?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Iranian legislative election]]
**Run-off [[Elections in Iran|parliamentary elections]] are being held in [[Iran]]. The first round of the election was held in February and provoked criticism as more than 7000 applicants got barred from participating. [https://www.foreignbrief.com/daily-news/iran-to-hold-run-off-parliamentary-elections/ (Foreign Brief)]
*Deputy Prime Minister of [[Samoa]] [[Fiame Naomi Mata'afa]] resigns over three proposed constitutional amendments, which would alter the power of the land and titles court. She also leaves the [[Human Rights Protection Party]]. Other MPs have already left the party over the issue and formed a new opposition party. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/425809/samoa-s-deputy-prime-minister-quits-cabinet-over-controversial-bills (RNZ)]
